detail.solution: Organized work into three phases with README-driven documentation, repeatable startup scripts, and consistent architecture patterns (React → Spring Boot → Python FastAPI ML service) reused across Phase 2 capstones.

projects.title: Smart Email Classification and Routing
projects.subtitle: NLP · ML microservices · Kanban dashboard
projects.description: Automates customer-support email triage — NLP preprocessing, dual Naive Bayes classifiers for category and priority, and a React Kanban dashboard backed by Spring Boot and FastAPI.
projects.stack: Python · FastAPI · Spring Boot · React · scikit-learn · NLTK · spaCy

detail.overview: A production-style, three-tier system that reads incoming customer emails, understands intent, and routes them automatically. Raw text flows through a six-step NLP pipeline (cleaning, tokenization, stopword removal, lemmatization, POS tagging, and NER), then through TF-IDF vectorization into two Multinomial Naive Bayes models — one for category (7 classes) and one for priority (Critical / High / Medium / Low). Results land on a React Kanban dashboard, sorted by urgency within each category column, with persistence via a Spring Boot REST API.
detail.problem: Support teams handling hundreds of daily emails face slow manual triage, inconsistent routing, mis-prioritization of urgent issues, and scaling limits as volume grows — agents spend time reading and sorting instead of resolving.
detail.solution: A Python FastAPI ML microservice (port 8000) handles preprocessing and inference; a Java Spring Boot API (port 8081) orchestrates classification, persists emails to JSON, and exposes REST endpoints; a React + Vite frontend (port 5173) provides a real-time Kanban board. The ML layer trains on 5,100 labeled support emails with an 80/20 stratified split, achieving 100% category accuracy on the test set and ~57% priority accuracy — expected given subjective priority labels.
features: Six-step NLP pipeline: lowercase cleaning, tokenization, stopword removal, lemmatization, POS tagging, and spaCy NER
TF-IDF vectorization (579 features) feeding dual Multinomial Naive Bayes classifiers for category and priority
FastAPI `/predict` endpoint returning category, confidence, priority, and processed text
Spring Boot REST API: classify, list, group-by-category, and delete emails with priority-aware sorting
React Kanban dashboard — seven category columns with color-coded priority badges and live routing feedback
Persistent storage with atomic ID sequencing; Critical emails always surface at the top of each column
Evaluated Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression, Linear SVM, and Random Forest — NB chosen for speed and probabilistic output
highlights: End-to-end story: raw text → NLP → ML → REST → dashboard — mirrors enterprise microservice patterns
Strong interview depth on TF-IDF, Naive Bayes assumptions, train/test splits, and honest accuracy trade-offs
Demonstrates full-stack skills aligned with HCL work: Spring Boot APIs, React UI, and Python ML services
Clear future scope documented: BERT fine-tuning, sentiment integration, PostgreSQL, JWT auth, and Docker deployment
Phase 2 capstone inside Agentic AI Learning — browse the parent repo for Phase 1 (Gemini chat) and Phase 3 (Java + Spring AI)
